newsitem.title: USA: Coastal Corp says await Iraq contract okay.
newsitem.headline: Coastal Corp says await Iraq contract okay.

text.p: Coastal Corp said Wednesday that it was waiting for U.S. Treasury approval of a contract it has signed with the Iraqi State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO).

Coastal spokesman William Osterloh declined to give details of the contract, which is one of a number of U.S. company oil contracts with Iraq pending approval by the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).
"Any (U.S.) oil firm that has signed an executory contract and agrees to abide by U.S. and U.N. rules will be approved," said Treasury spokesman Darren McKinney.

The contracts pending will be processed "as soon as physically possible" and forwarded to U.N. overseers "so as not to disadvantage U.S. companies," McKinney said, though he couldn't give a precise date.
Treasury is not currently disclosing details of the list of U.S. companies nor the details of pending Iraqi oil contracts, he added.

The United Nations said earlier Wednesday that it had still only received three contracts for approval, one of which has been approved. The Turkish state oil company TUPRAS's contract to lift 75,000 barrels per day (bpd) was approved on Tuesday. One of the contracts with the U.N. is thought to be the resubmitted one by Elf Aquitaine, which various well-placed U.N. sources said on Tuesday was rejected initially on a technicality.

The companies are looking to get a slice of the $2 billion of oil Iraq is allowed to sell over the next six months under the terms of a deal with the United Nations, with proceeds going to pay for humanitarian relief for Iraqi civilians and other Iraqi Gulf War obligations.
